newsitem.title: USA: Canadian official has "very good" talks on salmon.
newsitem.headline: Canadian official has "very good" talks on salmon.

text.p: U.S. and Canadian officials had "very good discussions" on Wednesday on a bitter dispute over fishing rights that threatened relations between the two close allies, Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said.
"We were able to look at the broad issues and see how we can take steps forward," he said after an hour-long meeting with U.S. officials including Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott.

Canadian fishermen held an Alaskan ferry hostage in Prince Rupert, British Columbia, for three days to protest against alleged U.S. overfishing of salmon in the Pacific, but allowed the vessel to leave late on Monday.
The Canadian fishermen contend that Alaskans have taken almost four times as much sockeye salmon this season as allowed under a 1985 Pacific Salmon treaty.
"I think we both genuinely feel that the treaty is very important," Axworthy told reporters. "To use that old expression, we had very good discussions."

Months of stormy talks between Canadian and U.S. officials on how to divide this year's Pacific salmon catch broke down last month. U.S. officials have denied breaching any international agreements and said Canada was responsible for the breakdown. Canadian fishermen have given the Ottawa government one week to make progress on resolving the dispute and threatened further action if it fails to do so.
